articles.title: Market Barriers Keep Biosimilars From Gaining Ground Against Brand-Name Rivals
articles.summary: This Q&A examines the persistent market and formulary barriers that prevent biosimilars from displacing high-cost brand-name biologics. For self-funded employers and PBMs, understanding these adoption hurdles is critical for unlocking potential specialty drug savings.
articles.source_line: Source: Managed Healthcare Executive; Wed, 14 Oct 2026 14:03:43 GMT

articles.title: Study Shows Non-Responding Patients Continue GLP-1 Therapy Despite Lack of Efficacy
articles.summary: A new study reveals that many patients who fail to experience meaningful weight loss or glycemic control on GLP-1 medications continue taking the costly drugs anyway. This highlights a significant cost-management challenge for self-funded employers covering obesity treatments without strict utilization management or stopping rules. Plan sponsors must implement tighter clinical oversight and outcomes-based management to prevent sustained spending on ineffective specialty therapies.
articles.source_line: Source: Insurance Business; Wed, 14 Oct 2026 11:46:38 GMT

articles.title: Federal Agencies Finalize Transparency in Coverage Rules for Health Plans
articles.summary: Federal departments have finalized new Transparency in Coverage rules, impacting health plans and issuers regarding public reporting requirements. This regulatory update directly affects self-funded employers and PBMs by establishing stricter compliance and data disclosure mandates for health plan pricing.
articles.source_line: Source: JD Supra; Wed, 14 Oct 2026 20:40:08 GMT

articles.title: Celltrion Nears Major US PBM Formulary Deals for Biosimilars Ahead of Q4
articles.summary: Celltrion is closing in on major US PBM formulary negotiations with anticipated contract signings in the fourth quarter. This development directly impacts self-funded employers by potentially expanding biosimilar market access, driving competition, and creating new opportunities to lower specialty drug costs.
articles.source_line: Source: BigGo Finance; Wed, 14 Oct 2026 02:26:00 GMT

articles.title: Pennsylvania AG Sues Over Alleged Insulin Price Manipulation
articles.summary: The Pennsylvania Attorney General has filed a lawsuit alleging collusion to artificially inflate insulin prices. This legal action highlights ongoing state-level scrutiny and antitrust concerns regarding drug pricing practices, which directly impact self-funded employers managing high-cost specialty medications like insulin.

articles.title: State Sues Insulin Manufacturers and PBMs Over Artificial Price Increases
articles.summary: A state attorney general has filed a lawsuit against major insulin manufacturers and pharmacy benefit managers, alleging collusion to artificially inflate drug prices. This litigation increases legal and regulatory scrutiny on PBM pricing models and rebate practices, carrying significant implications for self-funded employers seeking transparent drug costs.
articles.source_line: Source: Northeast Times; Wed, 14 Oct 2026 13:38:43 GMT
